lycaonia_739.name: Lycaonia
lycaonia_739.what: A region of south-central Asia Minor containing the cities of Lystra and Derbe.
lycaonia_739.today: The Konya plain in south-central Turkey.
key: Driven from Iconium, Paul and Barnabas fled to Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia (Acts 14).
After Paul healed a lame man, the crowd shouted in Lycaonian that the gods had come down (Acts 14).
The people called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes and tried to offer sacrifices to them (Acts 14).

melita_761.name: Malta
melita_761.what: A Mediterranean island south of Sicily where Paul was shipwrecked on his voyage to Rome.
melita_761.today: Malta, an island nation south of Sicily.
key: The ship carrying Paul ran aground, and all on board reached land safely (Acts 27).
The islanders showed unusual kindness, and Paul survived a viper's bite unharmed (Acts 28).
Paul healed the father of Publius, the island's chief man, and others who were sick (Acts 28).
After three months the travelers sailed on an Alexandrian ship that had wintered there (Acts 28).

meribah_783.name: Meribah
meribah_783.what: A place near Rephidim where Israel quarreled with Moses and tested the Lord over water.
meribah_783.today: Near Rephidim in the Sinai Peninsula; exact site unknown.
key: God brought water from the rock at Horeb, and Moses named the place Massah and Meribah (Exodus 17).
Moses' blessing on Levi recalls God contending with him at the waters of Meribah (Deuteronomy 33).

merom_785.name: Merom
merom_785.what: Waters in upper Galilee where Joshua defeated the northern Canaanite kings led by Jabin of Hazor.
merom_785.today: Exact site uncertain; likely springs in upper Galilee, northern Israel.
key: Jabin of Hazor and his allies camped together at the waters of Merom to fight Israel (Joshua 11).
Joshua attacked them suddenly at Merom, and the Lord gave them into Israel's hand (Joshua 11).
Israel hamstrung the enemy's horses and burned their chariots as the Lord had commanded (Joshua 11).

minnith_804.name: Minnith
minnith_804.what: An Ammonite town east of the Jordan, the limit of Jephthah's victory and known for its wheat.
minnith_804.today: Exact site unknown; east of the Jordan near Heshbon, Jordan.
key: Jephthah struck the Ammonites from Aroer to the neighborhood of Minnith, taking twenty cities (Judges 11).
Judah and Israel traded wheat of Minnith with Tyre (Ezekiel 27).

moriah_821.name: Moriah
moriah_821.what: The land and mountain where God tested Abraham by asking him to offer Isaac.
moriah_821.today: Traditionally the Temple Mount area of Jerusalem.
key: God told Abraham to offer Isaac on a mountain in the land of Moriah (Genesis 22).
The angel of the Lord stopped Abraham, and God provided a ram in Isaac's place (Genesis 22).
Abraham named the place The Lord Will Provide (Genesis 22).

most_holy_825.name: Most Holy
most_holy_825.what: Duplicate of the Most Holy Place entry, the inner room of the tabernacle.

most_holy_place_826.name: Most Holy Place
most_holy_place_826.what: The innermost room of the tabernacle, and later of the temple, where the ark of the covenant stood.
most_holy_place_826.today: No longer exists; the temple stood on the Temple Mount, Jerusalem.
key: A veil separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, where the ark was placed (Exodus 26).
The high priest entered behind the veil only once a year, on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16).
Solomon built the temple's Most Holy Place and overlaid it with fine gold (2 Chronicles 3).
When Jesus died, the temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom (Matthew 27).
Christ entered the holy places once for all by his own blood (Hebrews 9).

mount_halak_839.name: Mount Halak
mount_halak_839.what: A bare mountain in the south rising toward Seir, the southern limit of Joshua's conquest.
mount_halak_839.today: Likely Jebel Halaq in the northern Negev, southern Israel.
key: Joshua's conquest reached from Mount Halak in the south to Baal-gad in the north (Joshua 11).
Mount Halak is named again as the southern edge of the land whose kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).

mount_moriah_848.name: Mount Moriah
mount_moriah_848.what: The hill in Jerusalem where Solomon built the temple, on the threshing floor of Ornan.
mount_moriah_848.today: The Temple Mount in Jerusalem's Old City.
key: Abraham was sent to offer Isaac on a mountain in the land of Moriah (Genesis 22).
David bought Ornan's threshing floor and built an altar there to stop a plague (1 Chronicles 21).
Solomon began building the temple on Mount Moriah, where the Lord had appeared to David (2 Chronicles 3).

mount_nebo_849.name: Mount Nebo
mount_nebo_849.what: A mountain in Moab east of the Jordan, from which Moses viewed the promised land before he died.
mount_nebo_849.today: Jebel Nebo, northwest of Madaba, Jordan.
key: God told Moses to climb Mount Nebo, view Canaan, and die there on the mountain (Deuteronomy 32).
Moses climbed Nebo to the top of Pisgah, and the Lord showed him the whole land (Deuteronomy 34).
Moses died in Moab, and God buried him in a grave no one knows (Deuteronomy 34).

mount_of_olives_828.name: Mount of Olives
mount_of_olives_828.what: A ridge east of Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley.
mount_of_olives_828.today: The ridge facing the Old City of Jerusalem from the east.
key: David went up the Mount of Olives weeping as he fled from Absalom (2 Samuel 15).
Zechariah foresaw the Lord standing on the Mount of Olives as it splits in two (Zechariah 14).
Seated on the Mount of Olives, Jesus taught about the end of the age (Matthew 24).
After the Last Supper, Jesus went to the Mount of Olives to pray (Luke 22).
Jesus ascended to heaven from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1).

mount_zemaraim_859.name: Mount Zemaraim
mount_zemaraim_859.what: A hill in the hill country of Ephraim where King Abijah of Judah addressed Jeroboam's army.
mount_zemaraim_859.today: Exact site unknown; in the hill country near Bethel, West Bank.
key: Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim and rebuked Jeroboam and Israel for forsaking the Lord (2 Chronicles 13).
Though Jeroboam ambushed Judah, God gave Abijah's army victory over Israel (2 Chronicles 13).

nebaioth_881.name: Nebaioth
nebaioth_881.what: The desert territory of an Arabian tribe descended from Ishmael's firstborn son Nebaioth.
key: Nebaioth, Ishmael's firstborn son, gave his name to the tribe (Genesis 25).
Isaiah foresees the rams of Nebaioth accepted on God's altar (Isaiah 60).

netaim_889.name: Netaim
netaim_889.what: A village of Judah where potters in the king's service lived.
netaim_889.today: Exact site unknown; likely in the lowland of Judah.
key: Potters who worked for the king lived at Netaim and Gederah (1 Chronicles 4).
These potters belonged to the clans descended from Shelah son of Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

patmos_926.name: Patmos
patmos_926.what: A small rocky island in the Aegean Sea where John received the book of Revelation.
patmos_926.today: Patmos, a Greek island in the Dodecanese, Aegean Sea.
key: John was on Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus (Revelation 1).
In the Spirit on the Lord's day, John was told to write to seven churches (Revelation 1).
John saw the glorified Christ standing among seven golden lampstands (Revelation 1).

peniel_930.name: Peniel
peniel_930.what: A place by the Jabbok River where Jacob wrestled with God and was renamed Israel.
peniel_930.today: Likely Tell edh-Dhahab esh-Sharqi, on the Zarqa (Jabbok) River in Jordan.
key: Jacob wrestled with a man until daybreak and was renamed Israel (Genesis 32).
Jacob named the place Peniel, saying he had seen God face to face (Genesis 32).
The sun rose as Jacob passed Penuel, limping because of his hip (Genesis 32).

perez-uzzah_935.name: Perez-uzzah
perez-uzzah_935.what: The threshing floor where God struck Uzzah dead for touching the ark of the covenant.
perez-uzzah_935.today: Exact site unknown; between Kiriath-jearim and Jerusalem.
key: At Nacon's threshing floor Uzzah took hold of the ark, and God struck him down (2 Samuel 6).
David was angry and afraid, and named the place Perez-uzzah (2 Samuel 6).
Chronicles records the same event at the threshing floor of Chidon (1 Chronicles 13).

pergamum_937.name: Pergamum
pergamum_937.what: A leading city of the Roman province of Asia, home of one of the seven churches of Revelation.
key: Pergamum is one of seven churches John is told to write to (Revelation 1).
Christ says the church lives where Satan's throne is, yet held fast when Antipas was killed (Revelation 2).
He rebukes some there for holding the teaching of Balaam and the Nicolaitans (Revelation 2).
He promises the one who conquers hidden manna and a white stone (Revelation 2).

pethor_939.name: Pethor
pethor_939.what: Balaam's hometown near the Euphrates River in upper Mesopotamia.
pethor_939.today: Likely ancient Pitru, near Carchemish in northern Syria.
key: King Balak of Moab sent messengers to Balaam at Pethor to curse Israel (Numbers 22).
Moses recalls that Balaam son of Beor was hired from Pethor to curse Israel (Deuteronomy 23).

philadelphia_941.name: Philadelphia
philadelphia_941.what: A city in the Roman province of Asia, home of one of the seven churches of Revelation.
key: Philadelphia is one of seven churches John is told to write to (Revelation 1).
Christ says the church has kept his word and gives it an open door (Revelation 3).
He promises to keep them from the hour of trial coming on the world (Revelation 3).
The one who conquers will be made a pillar in the temple of God (Revelation 3).

pisidia_952.name: Pisidia
pisidia_952.what: A mountainous region of southern Asia Minor visited by Paul on his first missionary journey.
pisidia_952.today: The Taurus Mountains region of south-central Turkey.
key: Paul and Barnabas came to Antioch in Pisidia, and Paul preached in the synagogue (Acts 13).
Returning from Lystra and Iconium, they passed through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia (Acts 14).

place_954.name: Place of a Skull
place_954.what: The place just outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified, the meaning of the name Golgotha.
place_954.today: Traditionally at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Jerusalem.
key: Soldiers brought Jesus to Golgotha, the Place of a Skull, and crucified him there (Matthew 27).
Mark explains that Golgotha means Place of a Skull, where Jesus was crucified (Mark 15).

plain_of_jordan_654.name: Jordan Valley
plain_of_jordan_654.what: The well-watered lowland along the Jordan River near the Dead Sea, where Lot chose to settle.
plain_of_jordan_654.today: The Jordan Valley north of the Dead Sea, between Israel, the West Bank, and Jordan.
key: Lot saw that the Jordan Valley was well watered like the garden of the Lord (Genesis 13).
Lot chose the Jordan Valley and moved his tents as far as Sodom (Genesis 13).

pool_957.name: Pool of Shelah
pool_957.what: A pool by the king's garden in Jerusalem, likely the same as the Pool of Siloam.
pool_957.today: Likely the Pool of Siloam area, City of David, south of Jerusalem's Old City.
key: Shallun rebuilt the Fountain Gate and the wall of the Pool of Shelah (Nehemiah 3).
The rebuilt wall ran past the king's garden to the stairs down from the City of David (Nehemiah 3).

ramathaim-zophim_977.name: Ramathaim-zophim
ramathaim-zophim_977.what: A town in the hill country of Ephraim, home of Elkanah and Hannah and birthplace of Samuel.
ramathaim-zophim_977.today: Exact site debated; often linked with Ramah north of Jerusalem.
key: Elkanah, husband of Hannah, was from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim (1 Samuel 1).
After praying at Shiloh, Hannah returned home to Ramah and gave birth to Samuel (1 Samuel 1).
Samuel made Ramah his home, judged Israel there, and built an altar to the Lord (1 Samuel 7).

rehob_987.name: Rehob
rehob_987.what: An Aramean town and district in the far north of Israel, near Dan and Lebo-hamath.
rehob_987.today: Exact site unknown; near Dan in far northern Israel or southern Lebanon.
key: The spies explored the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, near Lebo-hamath (Numbers 13).
Laish, later Dan, lay in the valley belonging to Beth-rehob (Judges 18).
The Ammonites hired Syrians of Beth-rehob and Zobah to fight against David (2 Samuel 10).

rehob_988.name: Rehob
rehob_988.what: A town on the northern border of Asher's territory, listed toward Sidon.
rehob_988.today: Exact site unknown; in upper Galilee or southern Lebanon.
key: Rehob is listed on Asher's border with Hammon and Kanah, as far as Sidon (Joshua 19).
A second Rehob in Asher appears a few verses later near Aphek (Joshua 19).

rephaim_995.name: Rephaim
rephaim_995.what: A people group of tall early inhabitants; their land in Bashan is covered under Bashan.

rogelim_1012.name: Rogelim
rogelim_1012.what: A town in Gilead east of the Jordan, home of David's loyal supporter Barzillai.
rogelim_1012.today: Exact site unknown; in Gilead, northern Jordan.
key: Barzillai of Rogelim brought food and supplies to David at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt (2 Samuel 17).
Barzillai came down from Rogelim to escort the king across the Jordan (2 Samuel 19).

sea_of_the_plain_1035.name: Sea of the Arabah
sea_of_the_plain_1035.what: The salt lake at the south end of the Jordan Valley, today called the Dead Sea.
sea_of_the_plain_1035.today: The Dead Sea, between Israel, the West Bank, and Jordan.
key: Waters flowing toward the Sea of the Arabah were cut off as Israel crossed the Jordan (Joshua 3).
Jeroboam II restored Israel's border from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, as Jonah foretold (2 Kings 14).

sea_of_tiberias_1034.name: Sea of Tiberias
sea_of_tiberias_1034.what: Another name for the Sea of Galilee, taken from the city of Tiberias on its western shore.
sea_of_tiberias_1034.today: Lake Kinneret (the Sea of Galilee), northern Israel.
key: Jesus crossed the Sea of Galilee, also called the Sea of Tiberias, and fed five thousand (John 6).
The risen Jesus appeared by the Sea of Tiberias and gave the disciples a great catch (John 21).
After breakfast on the shore, Jesus three times asked Peter whether he loved him (John 21).

sela-hammahlekoth_1297.name: Rock of Escape
sela-hammahlekoth_1297.what: A rocky place in the Wilderness of Maon where Saul nearly caught David.
sela-hammahlekoth_1297.today: Exact site unknown; in the Wilderness of Maon south of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Saul's men were closing in on David on the other side of the mountain (1 Samuel 23).
Saul broke off pursuit to face a Philistine raid, so the place is called the Rock of Escape (1 Samuel 23).

smyrna_1103.name: Smyrna
smyrna_1103.what: A port city of the Roman province of Asia, home of one of the seven churches of Revelation.
key: Smyrna is one of seven churches John is told to write to (Revelation 1).
Christ knows the church's tribulation and poverty, yet says it is rich (Revelation 2).
He tells them to be faithful unto death and promises the crown of life (Revelation 2).

spain_1111.name: Spain
spain_1111.what: The Roman lands of the Iberian Peninsula at the western end of the Mediterranean.
spain_1111.today: Spain and Portugal, on the Iberian Peninsula.
key: Paul hoped to visit the Roman believers on his way to Spain (Romans 15).
After delivering the gift to Jerusalem, Paul planned to go by way of Rome to Spain (Romans 15).

taberah_1127.name: Taberah
taberah_1127.what: A wilderness camp where fire from the Lord burned among the complaining Israelites.
taberah_1127.today: Exact site unknown; in the wilderness between Mount Sinai and Kadesh.
key: When the people complained, fire from the Lord burned the outskirts of the camp (Numbers 11).
Moses prayed, the fire died down, and the place was named Taberah (Numbers 11).
Moses reminds Israel that they provoked the Lord at Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth-hattaavah (Deuteronomy 9).

tabor_1129.name: Tabor
tabor_1129.what: A town in Zebulun near Mount Tabor, given to the Merarite Levites.
tabor_1129.today: Exact site unknown; near Mount Tabor in northern Israel.
key: Zebulun's border ran by Chisloth-tabor, possibly the same town (Joshua 19).
Tabor and its pasturelands were given from Zebulun to the Merarite Levites (1 Chronicles 6).

tel-abib_1143.name: Tel-abib
tel-abib_1143.what: A settlement of Judean exiles by the Chebar canal in Babylonia, where Ezekiel lived.
tel-abib_1143.today: Exact site unknown; by the Chebar canal near Nippur, southern Iraq.
key: Ezekiel came to the exiles at Tel-abib by the Chebar canal and sat overwhelmed seven days (Ezekiel 3).
After seven days, God appointed Ezekiel a watchman for the house of Israel (Ezekiel 3).

thebez_1157.name: Thebez
thebez_1157.what: A town near Shechem where Abimelech was mortally wounded by a millstone a woman dropped.
thebez_1157.today: Likely Tubas, northeast of Nablus, West Bank.
key: Abimelech captured Thebez, but its people shut themselves inside a strong tower (Judges 9).
A woman dropped a millstone on Abimelech's head, and his armor-bearer killed him (Judges 9).
Joab expected David to recall Abimelech's death at Thebez when hearing of Uriah's death (2 Samuel 11).

tigris_1163.name: Tigris
tigris_1163.what: One of the two great rivers of Mesopotamia, named among the rivers flowing from Eden.
tigris_1163.today: The Tigris River, flowing through Turkey and Iraq.
key: The Tigris is the third river from Eden, flowing east of Assyria (Genesis 2).
Standing beside the Tigris, Daniel saw a glorious man clothed in linen (Daniel 10).

timnah_1165.name: Timnah
timnah_1165.what: A town in the hill country of Judah, distinct from the Timnah on Judah's northern border.
timnah_1165.today: Exact site uncertain; in the hill country of Judah, West Bank.
key: Possibly the Timnah where Judah went up to shear his sheep and met Tamar (Genesis 38).
Timnah is listed with Kain and Gibeah among the hill-country towns of Judah (Joshua 15).

timnath-serah_1167.name: Timnath-serah
timnath-serah_1167.what: Joshua's own town in the hill country of Ephraim, where he lived and was buried.
timnath-serah_1167.today: Likely Khirbet Tibnah, northwest of Bethel, West Bank.
key: Israel gave Joshua Timnath-serah at his request, and he rebuilt the town (Joshua 19).
Joshua was buried at Timnath-serah, north of the mountain of Gaash (Joshua 24).
Judges recalls his burial at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim (Judges 2).

tiphsah_1169.name: Tiphsah
tiphsah_1169.what: A town that King Menahem of Israel attacked brutally because it would not open its gates.
tiphsah_1169.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tappuah near Tirzah, West Bank.
key: Menahem seized Israel's throne by killing Shallum in Samaria (2 Kings 15).
He attacked Tiphsah brutally because it would not open its gates to him (2 Kings 15).

tishbe_1171.name: Tishbe
tishbe_1171.what: The hometown of the prophet Elijah, who is called the Tishbite.
tishbe_1171.today: Exact site unknown; traditionally in Gilead, northern Jordan.
key: Elijah the Tishbite, of Tishbe in Gilead, announced a drought to King Ahab (1 Kings 17).
God sent Elijah the Tishbite to confront Ahab over Naboth's vineyard (1 Kings 21).
King Ahaziah recognized from a description that the prophet was Elijah the Tishbite (2 Kings 1).

valley_of_beracah_1200.name: Valley of Beracah
valley_of_beracah_1200.what: A valley near Tekoa where Judah praised God after he defeated the invading armies.
valley_of_beracah_1200.today: Likely Wadi Berekut, near Tekoa south of Bethlehem, West Bank.
key: Jehoshaphat led Judah in prayer, and God made the invading armies destroy one another (2 Chronicles 20).
After three days of gathering spoil, Judah assembled in the valley and blessed the Lord (2 Chronicles 20).

valley_of_hamongog_1205.name: Valley of Hamon-gog
valley_of_hamongog_1205.what: A valley in Ezekiel's prophecy where the armies of Gog will be buried.
valley_of_hamongog_1205.today: A prophetic location east of the sea; no known site.
key: God gives Gog a burial place in the Valley of the Travelers, renamed Hamon-gog (Ezekiel 39).
Israel will spend seven months burying the dead to cleanse the land (Ezekiel 39).
Searchers mark any bone they find so buriers can carry it to the valley (Ezekiel 39).

valley_of_jehoshaphat_1209.name: Valley of Jehoshaphat
valley_of_jehoshaphat_1209.what: The valley where Joel foresees God gathering the nations for judgment.
valley_of_jehoshaphat_1209.today: Exact site unknown; traditionally the Kidron Valley east of Jerusalem.
key: God will gather all nations there and judge them for scattering his people Israel (Joel 3).
The nations are summoned to the valley, where God will sit to judge them (Joel 3).
Multitudes fill the valley of decision as the day of the Lord draws near (Joel 3).

valley_of_lebanon_1212.name: Valley of Lebanon
valley_of_lebanon_1212.what: The broad valley between the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon ranges, below Mount Hermon.
key: Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon marked the northern limit of Joshua's conquest (Joshua 11).
The valley is named again in the summary of kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).

valley_of_slaughter_1219.name: Valley of Slaughter
aka: Valley of the Son of Hinnom
valley_of_slaughter_1219.what: Jeremiah's name of judgment for the Valley of Hinnom, where children were sacrificed.
valley_of_slaughter_1219.today: The Hinnom Valley, south of Jerusalem's Old City.
key: Jeremiah condemned Topheth and said it would be called the Valley of Slaughter (Jeremiah 7).
Jeremiah broke a clay flask in the valley, repeating that it would be called the Valley of Slaughter (Jeremiah 19).

valley_of_sorek_1220.name: Valley of Sorek
valley_of_sorek_1220.what: A broad valley running west from the hills of Judah into Philistine territory.
valley_of_sorek_1220.today: Nahal Sorek, west of Jerusalem toward the coast, Israel.
key: Samson loved Delilah, who lived in the Valley of Sorek (Judges 16).
The Philistine lords paid Delilah to learn the secret of Samson's strength, and she betrayed him (Judges 16).

way_of_holiness_1231.name: Way of Holiness
way_of_holiness_1231.what: A prophetic highway in Isaiah on which God's redeemed people return to Zion.
way_of_holiness_1231.today: A prophetic image, not a known physical road.
key: Isaiah foresees a highway through the desert called the Way of Holiness (Isaiah 35).
The unclean will not travel it, and no lion or ravenous beast will be there (Isaiah 35).
The redeemed will walk it and return to Zion with singing and everlasting joy (Isaiah 35).

zanoah_1240.name: Zanoah
zanoah_1240.what: A town in the hill country of Judah, distinct from the Zanoah in the lowland.
zanoah_1240.today: Likely Khirbet Zanuta, southwest of Hebron, West Bank.
key: Zanoah is listed among Judah's towns in the hill country, near Jezreel and Kain (Joshua 15).
Jekuthiel is named as the father, likely the founder, of Zanoah (1 Chronicles 4).

zephath_1251.name: Zephath
zephath_1251.what: A Canaanite town in the Negev that Judah and Simeon destroyed and renamed Hormah.
zephath_1251.today: Exact site uncertain; in the northern Negev near Beersheba, Israel.
key: Judah and Simeon struck the Canaanites in Zephath and devoted it to destruction (Judges 1).
The city was then called Hormah (Judges 1).

zeredah_1254.name: Zeredah
zeredah_1254.what: A town in Ephraim, the hometown of Jeroboam, first king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
zeredah_1254.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly near Deir Ghassaneh in the hills of Samaria, West Bank.
key: Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, rebelled against King Solomon (1 Kings 11).
The prophet Ahijah told Jeroboam that God would give him ten tribes (1 Kings 11).

zin_1262.name: Zin
zin_1262.what: A desert region south of Canaan around Kadesh, forming the southern border of the land.
zin_1262.today: The desert of southern Israel and northeastern Sinai, near Kadesh-barnea.
key: The twelve spies began exploring Canaan from the wilderness of Zin (Numbers 13).
Miriam died at Kadesh in Zin, and Moses struck the rock at Meribah (Numbers 20).
Zin marked the southern border of Canaan and of Judah (Numbers 34).
Judah's southern boundary passed along the wilderness of Zin (Joshua 15).

ziph_1267.name: Ziph
ziph_1267.what: A town in the Negev of Judah toward Edom, distinct from Ziph near Hebron.
ziph_1267.today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev of southern Israel.
key: Ziph is listed among Judah's southernmost towns toward the border of Edom (Joshua 15).
A different Ziph appears later in the same list among the hill-country towns (Joshua 15).
